scope: Actual desktop Linux Chromium headless Rust/WASM browser checks. Not Android/mobile, recovery, real-time performance or physical qualification.

runtime.installation: Workspace-only unpack of official Debian chromium-headless-shell and matching chromium-common; no system installation or security-policy change

scenarios: Actual hand pull, mouse release, natural continuation
checks: Every served asset matches the captured built artifact hash

checks.name: pointercancel: physical continuation equals real mouse release despite stale held-button motion
blur: physical continuation equals real mouse release despite stale held-button motion
Reset leaves no phantom physical force after stale held-button movement

checks: Cancellation matches an actual released physical trajectory; continuing held-pull control diverges. This tests physical behavior, not pointer metadata alone.

webgpu.observation: At frame 30, canvas is blank despite successful adapter initialization and draw counters. No body, ground or striker is visible.

rawCanvasClear.failure: GPUQueue.onSubmittedWorkDone rejects: A valid external Instance reference no longer exists; device becomes destroyed

bufferWriteOnly.consequence: A buffer-only capability check would fail to detect the unusable canvas path

causalIsolation.inference: Failure is in this browser execution/presentation path: a raw JavaScript canvas clear reproduces it without application, wgpu, camera, depth, uniform or shader code. No renderer-layout defect was established.

manual.note: Native wall-time browser recording; explicit 4-tick/0.1-second manual simulation clock shown. Best complete regression clip.

automatic.note: Native automatic-scheduler browser recording; observed 0.325 simulated seconds over 2.128 wall seconds, not real-time performance admission.

sourceIdentityLimit: Source hashes are the regression script subset, not a full source-tree identity. Built asset hashes are authoritative for this run.

behavior: Before selecting WebGPU, clear a detached one-pixel WebGPU canvas and await completed GPU work with a five-second bound
Auto falls back to WebGL2 only when the render probe fails; capable WebGPU remains selectable
Explicit WebGPU reports a useful error with Auto/WebGL2 recovery choice
Detach retired canvas before destroying its device and ignore stale noncurrent-canvas context-loss events
rendererReadinessFix.artifactProvenanceLimit: Renderer-only browser tests used a copy of the prior built WASM bundle with the exact updated driver source and regenerated matching driver SRI hash. They are not a new full Trunk/WASM build or verification of concurrent physics changes. A final rebuilt application must be retested.

portableJavaScriptTests.note: Includes 13 readiness/renderer-selection tests, with deterministic mocked GPU success/failure/deadline and stale-canvas switching coverage; actual GPU/browser proof is recorded separately.
